# Serpentine belt and tensioner

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Consider Continental kits for value and note potential differences between aftermarket and OEM tensioner pulleys. [t303]

[Partial] Remove the drive belt from the engine pulleys, then inspect each pulley for side-to-side play. [t359]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the drive belt from the engine pulleys.
2. [Partial] Inspect each pulley for any side-to-side play or wobble.

## Tools

- [Partial] Air filter (implied) [t303]

## Parts

- [Partial] Continental Kit, Tensioner, Idler, Belt: $80 price point; includes Canadian-made parts; features a plastic pulley vs OEM metal [t303]
- [Partial] Dayco Tensioner: Alternative to OEM [t303]
- [Partial] Gates Belt: Used with Dayco tensioner and idler [t303]

## Tips & gotchas

- Listen for the operating sound of the throttle valve moving during the 10-second window after turning ignition OFF. [t22]
- [Partial] Perform this procedure each time the harness connector of the electric throttle control actuator or ECM is disconnected. [t22]
- Consider Continental kits for value at around $80. [t303]
- Note that some aftermarket tensioners use a plastic pulley compared to the painted metal OEM version. [t303]
